html:
Term Product NF Interpretation
(5) \varphi_0\sigma_0 \cdot \mathbf{1} \varphi_0\sigma_0 Horizontal passes through the bare core; unchanged.
(6) \varphi_0\sigma_0 \cdot \psi_0\sigma_0 \varphi_0\psi_0\,\mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\psi_0 h\,\sigma_0 Same-axis collision. The Hecke relation fires: \sigma_0^2 = h\sigma_0 + \mathbf{1}. Two horizontal polarizations partially annihilate back to vacuum (\mathbf{1}) and leave a residual polarization reduced by h.
(7) \varphi_0\sigma_0 \cdot \psi_1\sigma_1 \varphi_0\psi_1 L_+ Cross-polarization linking. Horizontal meets vertical and they combine into L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1 (closure in B_3: the unknot). No annihilation, no residual: the two polarizations combine into topology.
(8) \varphi_0\sigma_0 \cdot \psi_{01}V \varphi_0\psi_{01}\bigl(\sigma_1^{-1} + hV\bigr) = \varphi_0\psi_{01}\bigl(\sigma_1 + hL_+ - h^2\sigma_0 - h\,\mathbf{1}\bigr) Polarization meets the vertex. Via \sigma_0 \cdot \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_0^2\sigma_1^{-1} = (h\sigma_0 + \mathbf{1})\sigma_1^{-1}: the Hecke relation absorbs the \sigma_0 crossing, leaving the inverse orthogonal crossing \sigma_1^{-1} plus a residual vertex hV.
